Analysis and interpretation:
Strict maternal dose-productivity ordering across burden definitions
“Maternal greater” counts setting–horizon pairs in which the lowest mean maternal-only DALYs per additional discounted receipt exceeded the highest adolescent-only value. Seven settings and two horizons contribute 14 pairs; Sweden already had 90% adolescent coverage. YLL scale multiplies all mortality included in each setting. A second calculation scales infant YLL alone while retaining older-age mortality where included. These counts describe mean rankings; paired conditional frequencies and all strategy-level ratios are supplied in the source data.

Maternal dose-productivity ranking under infant-YLL scaling
“Maternal greater” counts setting–horizon pairs in which the lowest mean maternal-only health yield exceeds the highest adolescent-only yield per additional discounted administration. This table scales infant YLL while retaining older-age mortality where available.

Maternal-minus-adolescent health yield per 1,000 actual additional administrations
DALYs are discounted; the physical dose count is not. Each row compares the maternal alternative with the smallest mean yield against the adolescent alternative with the largest mean yield. Intervals use the paired clinical/cost draws for these fixed alternatives. Sweden has no adolescent expansion above its 90% baseline. The displayed setting-specific analysis uses all-age mortality in Brazil and Thailand and infant mortality elsewhere; the common primary cross-setting scope uses infant-only mortality in all eight settings.

Dose ranking under alternative morbidity definitions, mortality scopes and dose denominators
The comparison is strict: every maternal-only alternative must exceed every adolescent-only alternative in mean health yield. Discounted denominators sum added administrations with 3% annual discounting. Physical denominators sum the same administrations without discounting. Both numerators use discounted DALYs. These are administration counts, distinct from unique recipients, pregnancies and expenditure.

Alternative productivity denominators for the first feasible expansion
Twenty-year results compare the lowest available coverage increase separately for maternal (M) and adolescent (A) vaccination. The target-recipient denominator counts undiscounted vaccination episodes, while the health numerator remains discounted. The programme-expenditure denominator includes vaccine and delivery costs; net expenditure also includes treatment savings. No unique-woman denominator or equal-budget allocation is inferred.
